newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Petron to shut CDU Sept instead of Aug - source.
newsitem.headline: Petron to shut CDU Sept instead of Aug - source.

text.p: Philippines oil refiner Petron Corp has delayed the maintenance shutdown of its crude distillation unit (CDU) No.2 and reformer by a month to September 1-12, a company source said on Tuesday.
The turnaround of the 85,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) CDU -- to regenerate the catalyst in the 17,000-bpd reformer -- had been scheduled for August 1-12.
"It was delayed because about a month ago, it was decided the catalyst can still go," the source said.
This is the second time Petron has postponed the shutdown at its 155,000-bpd refinery in Bataan, north of the capital Manila.
The unit was originally planned to be shut in March, but the good condition of the catalyst delayed the maintenance to August.
The shutdown of the reformer, which produces reformate or unfinished gasoline, will now take place after Petron restarts its 15,000-bpd thermal cracker mid-August, the source said.
The cracker, the only damaged the unit from an explosion on June 20, produces diesel, gasoline and liquefied petroleum gas.
The unexpected shutdown of the cracker was partly behind Petron's issue last week of a gasoline import tender -- the first time it had issued such a tender in two years.
But the tender, which closed on July 18 and was valid for a day, was cancelled for operational reasons.
"The management needs to reassess the actual requirement ... the volume and quantity," he said.
The tender had sought 70,000 barrels of 95-octane unleaded gasoline for August 11-15 delivery to Bataan.
The source said alternatively, reformed naphtha or reformate with a 95 to 97-octane grade, was also being considered by Petron.
